title: Left for Dead on Everest, He Walked Into Camp #shorts
description:
Case 014. On 10 May 1996 Beck Weathers, a pathologist from Dallas, was climbing Mount Everest with Rob Hall's expedition when he found he could no longer see well enough to go on. He waited high on the mountain for most of the day. On the way down a blizzard caught his group, and they lost their way close to the tents of the high camp. Rescuers who reached them in the night judged him beyond help. The next morning a doctor from his team found him still breathing under a crust of ice and, with nothing that could be done for him there, had to leave him as well; his family was told he was dead. By his own account he was unconscious for about fifteen hours. That afternoon he woke with his right hand frozen solid, stood up and walked into camp. He was not expected to live through the night, and did. He was helped down to a lower camp, and a Nepalese army pilot, Lt. Col. Madan Khatri Chhetri, flew one of the highest helicopter rescues ever made to lift him off the mountain. He lost his right hand and part of the forearm, the fingers of his left hand, parts of both feet and his nose, which surgeons rebuilt. He went home to his family and wrote a book about it, Left for Dead. Eight climbers died on Everest in that storm. Rook didn't believe it either.

Animated reconstruction of a true story. The mountain, camps, tent, helicopter and house in the film are generic low-poly sets, not models of the real places or aircraft, and the cards on the case board are drawings made for it. Sources give different lengths for the time he lay in the snow (fifteen to eighteen hours); the film uses his own figure.
